evidence: "Once installed and paid for, a link can be used in any number of these paths"; gpt-oss-120b uses "dp = [[INF] * n for _ in range(1 << t)]" and "full = (1 << t) - 1" to combine requirements into one shared subgraph; deepseek-v4-flash computes all-pairs shortest paths before its subset optimization.
affordance_in_statement: Once a link is installed and paid for, it can be used in any number of these paths at no extra cost. The installed links do not need to form a single continuous line; they can form any network structure as long as the required paths exist within it.
removal_suggestion: Remove the explanatory optimization language and present validity only operationally: after selecting links, the resulting graph must satisfy the consecutive connectivity queries. Do not explicitly highlight that one installed link set may be reused across all paths or that arbitrary shared network structures are allowed.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Recognizes that all consecutive requirements can be satisfied by one shared connected subgraph and reduces the graph using shortest-path preprocessing followed by terminal-subset optimization.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: A single overall set of links must satisfy all requirements, and installed links can be reused in any number of paths.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Applies a Dreyfus-Wagner-style subset DP over the at most ten core banks to find a minimum shared Steiner network.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The installed links are paid for once and may support multiple paths; the core-bank count is bounded by t ≤ 10.

common_affordance: A single installed network may share edges and intermediate vertices among all consecutive core-bank paths.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: It treats each consecutive pair independently and effectively sums shortest-path costs, so it cannot exploit shared links between requirements.
It computes an MST over the entire graph rather than a minimum connected subgraph spanning only the required core banks, thereby including irrelevant vertices and missing the Steiner-tree objective.

recommended_edit: Re-present the shared-path condition indirectly as a graph-validity predicate: specify that the selected links must make each consecutive pair connected in the resulting graph, but remove the sentences explicitly emphasizing reuse, arbitrary network structure, and one common set of links. This preserves the mathematical task while withholding the direct Steiner-tree cue.
regression_risk: The edit may make qwen3-coder appear correct on instances where consecutive shortest paths do not share useful links, and may make glm-5 appear correct on instances where the full-graph MST happens to span the required cores optimally.
